criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test`. A new test records an intervention against a landed job and shows `athena status` listing it as open work, with its id, category and a next command. A second new test shows it disappears from open work once a later job's request cites its id.
criteria.evidence: I ran the new tests and all passed. `status_lists_an_uncited_intervention_as_open_work_with_a_next_command` lands a job, records a corrected-output intervention against it with `--job latest`, and asserts the id, category, job and the exact next command. It also asserts that the command appears in `status.next`. `an_intervention_leaves_open_work_once_a_later_request_cites_its_id` shows that an unrelated request leaves the intervention listed and a request naming the id removes it. The CLI test `the_status_command_lists_an_uncited_intervention_and_drops_it_once_cited` checks the same list-then-drop behavior through the real binary, in both text and `--json` output. Athena's full `cargo test --locked` run also passed (721 tests).

criteria.criterion: The status view has a distinct open-interventions list (id, what, category, next command). Its entries also appear in `next`, so a reader sees what to run without opening records.
criteria.evidence: In status.rs, `StatusView.open_interventions: Vec<OpenIntervention>` holds id, what, category, job and next. `status()` adds each entry to `next` as `athena ask "<request that addresses intervention ID>"   # follow up intervention ID (category)`. In display.rs the text output gets a `follow-up` line. I confirmed in crates/athena-cli/src/main.rs that `athena ask` takes the request as a positional argument, so the command form works.

criteria.criterion: An intervention cited by a later job is not listed. The rule for 'cited' is documented in a doc comment and in docs where status is described.
criteria.evidence: The filter in `open_interventions()` drops an intervention when a request job's `received_at` is at or after the intervention's `at` and its request text contains the intervention id. The rule is documented in the doc comment on `open_interventions`, in the doc comment on `Intervention` in records.rs, and in a new section of docs/records.md, "Following up an intervention". The `Intervention` record has no follow-up or citing field (records.rs lines 802-813), so request text is a reasonable link to use.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`. Both are clean.
criteria.evidence: Clippy finished with no warnings, and `cargo fmt --check` printed nothing.

criteria.criterion: The existing counts under 'interventions' (by category and class) are unchanged. Status for a repository with no interventions shows no new open work.
criteria.evidence: The diff does not touch `by_category` or `by_class`. The tests check that `interventions_by_category` is still 1 both before and after the intervention is cited. Both tests also check the empty case: `open_interventions.is_empty()` on a fresh repository, and no `follow-up` text before any intervention exists.

findings.summary: No test covers the rule that excludes interventions Athena observed itself.
findings.evidence: `open_interventions` filters on `source == InterventionSource::User`, but every new test uses user interventions. If that filter were removed, no test would fail.

findings.summary: The list of request jobs is rebuilt once for every intervention.
findings.evidence: `records.request_jobs()` is called inside the filter closure, so it collects and sorts the jobs again for each intervention. Building it once before the loop would avoid that work.

summary: The change fixes m6 from the acceptance review. `athena status` now lists each user-recorded intervention that no later request names by id under open work, with its id, category, description and an `athena ask` command. The same command is added to `next`, and the JSON output gains an additive `open_interventions` field. The existing intervention counts are unchanged, a repository with no interventions shows no new open work, and the rule for "cited" is documented in doc comments and in docs/records.md. I ran the new unit and CLI tests, clippy and fmt, and all were clean. Every changed file is on the expected deliverables list. One minor gap: no test covers excluding interventions Athena observed itself (source `observed`).
